content.title: Saks' bankruptcy filing creates uncertainty for iconic stores, suppliers and shoppers
content.summary: An appeal for bankruptcy protection filing of the operator of Saks Fifth Avenue, Bergdorf Goodman and Neiman Marcus has left the luxury department stores' suppliers with unpaid bills and caused a rift with Amazon, one of Saks Global's minority investors.  Saks Global said last week it had secured roughly $1.75 billion to help finance the company toward hoped-for profitability.  While the retailer's stores remain open for now, the bankruptcy and restructuring could likely impact the assortment of designer brands customers find online or in their local Neiman Marcus or Saks, according to industry experts.

content.title: European Indexes Bounce on Trump Tariff Climbdown
content.summary: European indexes opened to a sea of green, recouping some of this week's losses after President Donald Trump backtracked on his threats to impose tariffs in relation to his plan to control Greenland. Sectors that investors expected tariffs to hit most severely, such as luxury and auto makers, gained.

content.summary: Kering announced that Bartolomeo Rongone will step down as Bottega Veneta’s CEO on March 31, 2026, and appointed former Gucci Japan president Daniele Zito as its new group chief commercial officer with immediate effect. content.title: LVMH, Kering, and Other Luxury Stocks Sell Off on Tariff Concerns
content.summary: President Donald Trump’s renewed tariff threats were weighing on European luxury stocks Tuesday morning.  Over the weekend, Trump said he would impose a 10% tariff on eight European countries—Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, and Finland—to pressure them to allow the U.S. to buy Greenland.  The president later threatened to impose 200% tariffs on French wine and champagne.
